A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of ZDV in HIV/HCV‐coinfected individuals receiving PEG‐IFR/RBV therapy is associated with a greater decline in haemoglobin levels, a greater need for RBV dose reduction, and a greater need for erythropoietin therapy.
the use of ZDV in patients with HCV/HIV coinfection is associated with an increased rate of anaemia and RBV dose reductions, but is not associated with a decreased rate of virologic response.

the use of ZDV is associated with an increased incidence of anaemia during HVC therapy in HIV/HCV‐coinfected individuals, but the use of Zidovudine is not associated with a decreased rate of treatment discontinuation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ZDV use, not weight‐based dosing of RBV, is associated with an increased incidence of anaemia in HIV/HCV‐infected patients treated for chronic HCV infection.
the use of ZDV, but not weight‐adjusted RBV dosing, is associated with an increased incidence of anaemia during peginterferenceon/ribavirin treatment in HIV/hepatitis C‐coinfected individuals.
